news.title: Premier League to adopt major rules seen at 2026 FIFA World Cup: 5-sec countdown, 1-min injury ban and mo
news.lede: The 2026/27 Premier League season will bring several changes to how matches are restarted, substitutions are handled, injured players return to the field and certain red-card decisions are reviewed by VAR. Alongside those mandatory changes to the Laws of the Game, the Premier League has also published its ‘Football Principles’ and ‘Refereeing Points of Emphasis’ for the new campaign, setting out how referees and VAR officials are expected to approach a range of situations. Football News: The Premier League is set to implement significant rule changes for the 2026/27 season, including a five-second countdown for throw-ins, a one-minute injury protocol, and enhanced VAR interventions. These changes aim to reduce time-wasting and improve match efficiency.

news.title: Six post-World Cup transfers that caught our eye: Vozinha, Torres, Spence...
news.lede: Four weeks have passed since the World Cup final and plenty of players from the tournament have been making moves since then. It happens every four years. The World Cup is the perfect stage for a player to put themselves in the spotlight and attract new suitors at club level. This summer has been no different, with several protagonists from the World Cup making moves since.

news.title: ‘This is probably my last year in football,’ says Cristiano Ronaldo
news.lede: RIYADH — Cristiano Ronaldo says this Saudi Pro League season is likely to be the last of his professional career. The 41-year-old superstar’s contract with Riyadh club Al-Nassr, signed in December 2022, expires next June, and he has told Vogue magazine that another is unlikely. “This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” Ronaldo said. The Portugal forward, who has scored 976 career goals, married long-time partner, Georgina Rodriguez, earlier this month.

news.title: How 2026 World Cup, blockbuster movies are bringing old video games back
news.lede: Hyderabad: To call EA’s FC 26 disappointing would be an understatement. These days, the once-popular annual franchise barely sputters on as players search for joy in other genres and kinds of play. The step away from sports games is such that it is not just EA that is struggling, but also long-time rivals Konami (makers of PES and now eFootball) and 2K (NBA and WWE). With a steady decline in player numbers year after year and their refusal to engage with the game over the duration of a year, the outlook seemed grim.

news.title: Send us your Scotland World Cup memories of Boston
news.lede: Scotland played their first two World Cup group games in Boston. BBC Scotland is again looking for Scotland fans to send us in their footage, audio and pictures - this time capturing the memories from Boston during the World Cup. Thousands of Tartan Army supporters descended on the city and a relationship to last well beyond the World Cup was born. We are looking for Scotland fans to send us their videos, audio and memories of that magical week or so in Boston.

news.title: Two More African Nations Qualify for the Women's World Cup
news.lede: Two more African nations have qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup following the conclusion of the play-in round in this year's Women's African Cup of Nations. The play-in round featured all four nations that were eliminated in the quarter-final stage of the tournament, including the defending African champions, Nigeria, who faced off against the 2022 winners, South Africa. Across the bracket, the Ivory Coast looked to secure their place in the World Cup as they took on Ghana. Here is how the play-in matches unfolded:.
